summary.overview: The project ships well-navigated agent guidance (root AGENTS.md plus a docs/agents/ split, CONTEXT.md and ~90 ADRs), a broad test suite (538 test files), and four CI workflows including a PR-evidence acceptance gate. No eligible sessions were available in the 30-day window, so behavioral claims about editing, validation, and friction were not assessed and stay in the evidence boundary. One present issue was found: the repository root accumulates throwaway scratch and per-task worktree directories that .gitignore does not cover, which misdirects tooling and risks accidental staging.

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: Layered instructions, a domain glossary, and ADR records make the intended scope and authoritative context explicit, though no task episode was available to exercise them.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: A worktree gate script and build manifests give supported startup routes, but the filesystem cleanup boundary is deficient: recurring scratch and worktree residue in the repo root is not covered by ignore rules.

dimensions.label: Change Validation
dimensions.summary: A large tracked test suite and path-correlated source/test co-changes provide a relevant verification route; no session evidence was available to confirm it is exercised after edits.

dimensions.label: Reliable Delivery
dimensions.summary: CI and a PR-evidence acceptance workflow with a documented ruleset gate define the delivery boundary; the current review opened no real acceptance decision for a specific revision.

dimensions.label: Learning Capture
dimensions.summary: A bounded review completed with clean asset and memory integrity, but zero eligible episodes block any repeat, maintenance, or effectiveness conclusion; the gap stays an evidence boundary, not a finding.

findings.title: Throwaway scratch and worktree folders in the repo root misdirect tooling and risk accidental staging
findings.reason: The repository root accumulates a large set of untracked throwaway directories from prior tasks: temporary probe/repro trees (.tmp-*, including a bundled Python virtualenv at .tmp-921-dev/ocrenv), verification captures (.ci-verify/), handoff notes (.dsh-handoff/), spreadsheet extracts (xl/), and roughly a dozen per-task worktrees (wt-*, wtx-*, .wt-*). None of these are matched by the root .gitignore, so git status reports 169 untracked entries and any git add -A from the root would stage them. The consequence is already observable in tooling: the diff-impact scan grades the working tree as critical from ~5,556 changed files that are almost entirely these residue paths, and automated core/verification targeting anchors on throwaway content (repro .mjs files as 'source', vendored colorama/tests as the validation target, .ci-verify/*.png as recommended reads) instead of the backend/ and frontend/ implementation. The .gitignore already carves out .scratch/ and .workbuddy/ as non-committed working areas, so the same intent for these recurring classes is a proven wiring gap, not a new policy.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Config owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Extend the repository-root .gitignore so the recurring throwaway and per-task-worktree classes are excluded, mirroring the existing .scratch/ and .workbuddy/ carve-outs. Add ignore patterns for the observed classes (.tmp-*/, .ci-verify/, .dsh-handoff/, .dsh-*/, wt-*/, wtx-*/, .wt-*/, xl/) as separate lines with a short comment; do not weaken any existing rule and do not delete or move any directory. These paths are currently untracked, so no tracked file changes.

## Validation

- Run `git check-ignore .tmp-921-dev wt-1240 xl .ci-verify` from the repo root and confirm each now resolves to an ignore rule
- Run `git status --porcelain` and confirm the untracked entry count drops and no residue directory is listed for staging
- Run `git ls-files` and confirm none of these paths were previously tracked (expected: still zero)
